headline: GAAP profit swings positive as adjusted earnings advance
summary_short: Brighthouse Financial swung to net income of $956 million ($16.53/diluted share) in Q2 2026, reversing a $792 million Q1 GAAP loss, as adjusted earnings rose 8% q/q and 30% y/y to $258 million ($4.45/share) with the $70.00/share Aquarian Capital deal still pending.
summary_long: GAAP results reflect market-sensitive derivative and market-risk-benefit accounting, not the underlying business: net derivative losses narrowed to $477M from $1,237M a year ago, and a $1,370M favorable change in market risk benefits reversed Q1's $748M unfavorable swing, producing $956M net income versus a $792M Q1 loss. Adjusted earnings, which exclude that volatility, rose 8% q/q and 30% y/y to $258M, led by Annuities segment earnings of $349M on higher net investment income and record $2.1B Shield Level Annuity sales; total annuity sales fell 7% q/q on lower fixed-annuity volume. Cash rose to $7.1B and equity to $6.6B; combined RBC ratio held at 430%-450%, the upper end of target. The pending $70.00/share Aquarian Capital acquisition awaits remaining state insurance approvals.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the headline profit swing entirely to hedge/GAAP-reserve accounting volatility, not core-business growth; the pending $70/share Aquarian Capital all-cash buyout remains subject to remaining state insurance approvals.

GAAP revenue's q/q and y/y increases are almost entirely arithmetic: net derivative losses narrowed to $477M from $509M q/q and from $1,237M y/y, the largest single revenue-line mover; premiums, fees and net investment income were comparatively stable.

Swing to profit is arithmetically explained by a $1,370M favorable change in market risk benefits (vs Q1's $748M unfavorable change) plus derivative losses narrowing; company states it expects net-income volatility from hedge-target/GAAP-reserve differences tied to market performance.

Diluted EPS moves in lockstep with net income available to shareholders on an essentially flat 57.84M weighted diluted share count q/q and y/y, so the swing is fully attributable to the net-income change above.

Pretax income mirrors the net-income swing ahead of the statutory tax provision; the same market-risk-benefit change and narrower derivative losses are the dominant components per the condensed statement of operations.

Company attributes the increase to higher Annuities segment earnings ($349M, on higher net investment income) and a narrower Run-off segment loss ($56M vs $83M y/y), partially offset by a wider Corporate & Other loss.
Adjusted EPS growth mirrors adjusted earnings growth on a nearly flat diluted share count (57.84M vs 57.33M q/q, 57.73M y/y); no notable items affected either the current or year-ago quarter.

Equity growth is consistent with the quarter's $981M of net income attributable to Brighthouse being largely retained (retained deficit narrowed from -$1,452M to -$471M) plus a modest AOCI improvement.
not explained in the release; balance was unchanged q/q at $3,154M and essentially flat y/y.
Growth reflects the equity increase divided by an essentially flat share count (57.51M vs 57.12M shares outstanding y/y); not separately explained in the release.
Book value excluding AOCI rose from $8,231M to $8,977M on the same flat share count; not separately explained in the release.
Company states the ratio was consistent with Q1 2026 and at the upper end of its 400%-450% target range in normal markets.
